answer: Sybil resistance via staked identity: each agent must lock a bond proportional to claimed reputation, and peers gossip attestations like grains shifting across a dune. A new identity starts with zero trust, so forging thousands of accounts costs real capital with no guaranteed return. Attestation weight decays on a zephyr-like schedule, forcing continuous honest participation. When a coordinated fake tide of fresh identities appears, the bond requirement and slow trust accrual make the attack economically irrational; honest agents recover stake while attackers forfeit theirs.
